Explainer themes

Twenty-five draft design languages, including three Catppuccin flavors and twelve editor color schemes. Same sample in each.

My top three for you

  1. Inkwell. It looks like your own notebook. Your drawings fit without redrawing, and the green highlighter is a mark people will remember.
  2. Whiteprint. The best fit for low-level and CI topics. Exact lines suit memory layouts and pipelines, and engineers trust it on sight.
  3. Two-Ink. The most recognizable in a feed. Navy and pink read well in 9:16 reels and look like nobody else's AI output.

If you want one house look, take Inkwell and borrow Whiteprint's grid for dense diagrams. Skip Dry Erase as a signature: it is pleasant but common. Phosphor and Slate are dark only on purpose, so the toggle does not change them.

New: Catppuccin. The open-source (MIT) pastel palette, using only its official colors, checked against the @catppuccin/palette package v1.8.0. Catppuccin switches between Latte (light) and Mocha (dark) with the toggle. Frappé and Macchiato are the other two dark flavors. A good fit for agent and tooling topics, since many readers already use it in their editor.

New: Editor color schemes. Twelve schemes from the list in Nathan Long, "Colorschemes for the discerning developer": Rosé Pine, Tokyo Night, Dracula, Nord, Solarized, Oceanic Next, Tomorrow, Iceberg, One Half, Kanagawa, OneDark and Gruvbox. Every color comes from the scheme's own source palette, and each CSS file names the source file and license. Nord and Oceanic Next are dark only, since their sources define no light palette. The others switch between their light and dark variants with the toggle.
